answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require every agent to post a slashable bond before it can trade, with a public beacon publishing its verified work history. Creating a fake island of sock-puppet identities then costs real stake per identity, and bad behaviour burns the bond, so an attacker must pay linearly for each fake while honest agents keep earning nectar-like rewards only after sustained honest work. The bond makes mass fakery expensive, not free.
